title: Reserved capacity degradation: corrective runbook + targeted hotfix
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Summary: During a multi-customer spike on 2026-02-18 we observed sustained reserved pool depletion and degraded burst behavior for several enterprise tenants. Symptoms: autoscaler did not add capacity fast enough, burst allocation throttled earlier than expected, and KV cache warming caused unexpectedly high token generation per-request leading to capacity starvation. This ticket consolidates the immediate mitigations, the short-term hotfix we are implementing, and the permanent work to prevent recurrence.

Observed impact and scope:
- Affected customers: three Dedicated customers in us-west (NIM-Analytics, ArborPay, SiloMed). Customers experienced increased tail latency (p95 > 800ms -> > 2s) and intermittent 503s for burst requests.
- Duration: first signs 2026-02-18 03:10 UTC; majority of mitigations applied 2026-02-19 09:00 UTC.
- Root-cause hypothesis (summary): autoscaler decision logic used a 5m rolling average of GPU utilization and request rate, which under-weighted recent burst ramp because of a config change to kv_cache_ttl that temporarily increased per-request compute (KV misses), inflating per-token work and reducing effective capacity. Additionally, burst-reserve accounting had a bug which double-counted teardown windows, reducing available burstable capacity by ~18%.

Actions taken so far (what fixed the immediate outage):
1) Emergency mitigations (2026-02-19):
   - Reverted kv_cache_ttl experiment to previous value to reduce cold-KV misses (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4112).
   - Rolled forward a temporary autoscaler override to treat 30s recent surge weight as 60% of decision input (config flag autoscale_surge_weight) to react faster to ramps.
   - Manually increased reserved pool for the three affected customers by 20% (customer-facing change tracked in billing & provisioning).
2) Short-term hotfix (in-progress):
   - Code fix for burst-reserve accounting to stop double-counting teardown windows (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/control-plane/pull/1024). Target merge and canary rollout 2026-03-11.
   - Add metric autoscaler.rule_latency_seconds and alert where > 250ms (Grafana: https://grafana.internal/redwood/d/7aR/autoscaler-overview).

Planned permanent work (postmortem level):
- Replace 5m-only autoscaler input with a multi-window policy (15s/60s/5m) that uses an exponential weighting to capture fast ramps without overreacting to noise. Implementation: ENG-17390.
- Integrate KV cache health into autoscale decisions: expose kv_cache_miss_rate per model to the autoscaler so effective per-request work is estimated, not assumed.
- Add simulation harness to test reserve accounting against synthetic burst traces (ENG-17410).
- Improve customer-facing capacity APIs so we can advertise predictable burst guarantees and programmatically request emergency burst increases.

Communication and follow-up:
- Customer communication: sent technical incident updates to affected customers (thread IDs: CS-5483, CS-5491). Action items for SE/Sales: schedule follow-up calls to review postmortem and credits.
- Internal: incident review scheduled for 2026-03-16. Postmortem doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OPS/2026-02-18+-+Reserved+Pool+Degradation.

Acceptance criteria for closing this ticket:
- Hotfix merged and canary rolled with no regression in 72h.
- Autoscaler surge-weight metric and alerting in prod for 14 days with no sustained false positives.
- Follow-up RFC for multi-window autoscaler drafted and reviewed (at least 2 approvers from infra/serving).
- Customer follow-ups completed and credits approved where applicable.

Notes and trade-offs considered:
- We intentionally avoided immediately increasing autoscale aggressiveness cluster-wide to prevent oscillation and overspend for non-enterprise customers. Instead we used per-customer reserved pool increases.
- Longer-term integration of KV cache metrics into autoscaling requires additional telemetry that we decided to scope into a separate project to avoid delaying the hotfix.
